In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
discriminative training of recurrent neural networks with Mel-frequency features is the current state-of-the-art for time-frequency mask estimation in single-channel speech separation.
discriminative training of recurrent DNNs in a Mel feature space is the best approach for speech separation with DNNs, but that there is still a significant room for further improvement.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DNNs are a powerful tool for speech separation, but the choice of the training criteria and feature representation is critical for achieving the best results.
the best results are obtained when using discriminative training and long short-term memory DNNs in the Mel domain.
DNN-based speech separation is a promising direction, which is worth to be further investigated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DNNs are a viable approach to single-channel speech separation, and can achieve performance comparable to non-negative matrix factorizations, which are currently the state of the art in this task.
DNN-based speech separation is not limited to a specific feature representation and that the choice of the training criterion is more important for performance.
discriminatively trained recurrent DNNs can outperform state-of-the-art non-negative matrix factorizations and other deep learning approaches for single-channel speech enhancement.
